source: RFC-0007 Appendix C.1 and C.4.1; slice 1 shipped the signal tables and the forbidden list; slice 1G fills gh_read_allowlist and policy_set and adds consent_groups, agent_permission_denies, agent_permission_exempt, agent_mcp_denies and gh_notes; slice 2a fills isolation_vars and adds gate_rules, plugin defaults, consent_groups[].rev and per-class group/hint

isolation_markers.name: GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n/GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n
isolation_markers.value: an entry Carter's isolation block sets, e.g. the value no_push or a gpg.*program set to the resolved false

forbidden.note: `-n` is forbidden for `commit` only (it means `--no-verify` there; `merge -n` is `--no-stat`). Bare `-S` is never used: at T2 the LLM key signs through the environment.
forbidden.hint: Commit with plain `git commit -m <message>`: no `--no-verify`, signing, sign-off or author flags (Carter sets the identity).
Stage explicit paths: `git add <path>...`, never everything at once.
There is no push from an agent shell. Write the handoff file and ask the human to run `carter push`, then `carter pr`, in their own terminal.

forbidden.note: Forbidden as a `VAR=` prefix, with `env`/`env -u`, `unset` and `export`.
forbidden.hint: Do not set, export or unset identity, git config, SSH, HOME or Carter variables on a command.

forbidden.note: Any write at any scope is forbidden; only `--get*`, `--list` and `--show-*` pass.
forbidden.hint: Reading git config is fine (`git config --get <key>`); writing it is human-only.
Do not pass `-c` or `--config-env` for hook, signing, credential, URL, remote, user or Carter keys.

forbidden.note: `update-ref` is forbidden with a raw SHA.
forbidden.hint: Low-level history commands (`commit-tree`, `update-ref`, `filter-branch`, ...) are not available to agents.

forbidden.note: `docker` and `podman` belong to consent group `sudo-docker`; `gh` is limited to the read allowlist and a leading `gh -R` is refused.
forbidden.hint: This command is not available to agents (privilege, scheduling, nested OpenCode or the GitHub API). Ask the human.
That Carter command is human-only. Ask the human to run it in their own terminal.

forbidden.note: Any token that references `credential_paths` after normalization.
forbidden.hint: Credential locations are off limits from the shell; do not read them.

forbidden.note: Write-capable references to `control_paths`: redirections (`>`, `>>`) and these commands, or interpreter args naming them.
forbidden.hint: Carter's own control files cannot be written from the shell.

gh_notes.leading_repo_flag: A leading `gh -R/--repo` matches no allow statement, so it fails closed; the gate (2a) rejects it with 'put -R after the subcommand'. No statement carries -R.
gh_notes.api: `gh api` is never allowed: it is covered by the `deny-gh` statement and no allow matches it.
gh_notes.positional: `gh repo view` and `gh search repos` take the repository or query positionally: write `gh repo view <owner>/<repo>` and `gh search repos <query>`, never `-R` (spike 4: `unknown shorthand flag: 'R'`). `gh pr`, `gh issue` and `gh run` verbs take `-R <owner>/<repo>` after the subcommand.
gh_notes.dropped: `gh status` is not allowlisted: with a fine-grained read-only token it fails with HTTP 403 `Resource not accessible by personal access token` (spike 4).

consent_groups.effect: agents can't push or write to GitHub from their shell (gh is read-only); per-agent carter_push/carter_pr denies (devops keeps them: every use asks you first); the Carter plugin isolates every agent shell and gates its commands
explain: g2 now also installs the Carter plugin for OpenCode. It changes every agent shell:
- no SSH agent: agents cannot use your keys; git talks HTTPS with a read-only GitHub token (or none)
- no push and no GitHub writes: a command gate rejects them, with a message that says why
- commits made by agents are unsigned (they are blocked if your configured tier needs signing)
It does NOT change your own terminal or the `!` shell of OpenCode.
Recorded in ~/.carter/guard-state.json (group g2, revision 3) and ~/.carter/isolation.json.
Undo: `carter guard remove --only plugin` (keeps the other guards). If carter is broken: delete
~/.config/opencode/plugins/carter (a running OpenCode drops the plugin within seconds).
Restart the OpenCode server after installing so that it loads the plugin.
Revision 3 adds two tools for the devops agent only, `carter_push` and `carter_pr`: devops can propose
a push of the current branch to your SSH origin, or a pull request from its handoff file. You approve
every single use in the OpenCode prompt; your SSH agent is used only for that approved push.
B is a convenience, not a security boundary: an agent that deliberately tampers with your user account
could misuse it (until the sandbox). Undo B only: `carter guard remove --only broker`.

consent_groups.effect: agent pushes are blocked and agent commits are checked (identity, signature, trailer) in every repo on this machine, by git hooks in ~/.carter/hooks/carter-guard; your own commits and pushes are unaffected
explain: hooks now also checks agent commits (revision 2), in every repo on this machine:
- prepare-commit-msg: rejects an agent commit with the wrong committer or signing settings
and adds the Co-authored-by (or Assisted-by) trailer
- commit-msg: checks the trailer is there; post-commit: warns about an unsigned commit
It does NOT run for your own terminal: a human commit makes no git call and no extra command.
Undo: `carter guard remove --only hooks`.

consent_groups.effect: agents can't run sudo/docker; Packer docker builds must be typed in your terminal
agents can't read SSH keys, gh/git credentials or the read-only token, and can't edit ~/.ssh
agents can't edit OpenCode config, git hooks and config, or Carter's own config and control files
optional: adds the git alias `git ai-commit` (runs `carter commit`) to Carter's git config; never set if you already have an alias.ai-commit
explain: alias adds `git ai-commit` = `carter commit` (commits as the LLM identity, never as you).
It is optional and never part of a bare --yes. Undo: `carter guard remove --only alias`.

consent_groups.effect: git older than 2.54 only: the same push and commit guards as hook files in your repos (this one and your workspaces); hooks you or your tools own are never edited
explain: repo_hooks now also writes the commit hooks (revision 2): prepare-commit-msg, commit-msg and
post-commit, next to pre-push, in the repos where Carter owns the hook files (never over yours).

agent_mcp_denies.note: C14: the Carter GitHub MCP server (carter-github, tools carter_github_*) is hidden from roles that do not need it. The role list is a product decision to confirm.

policy_set.rfc: 4.5 gh deny-by-default; the read allowlist lifts it
4.5 read denies (the PAT file); C.1 credential_paths
4.5 edit denies (global opencode config; the glob also covers .jsonc and Carter's backups)
4.5 edit denies, D48 (project opencode.json; no leading slash so a Location-relative path matches too)
4.5 control plane, D61 (the file and its gitconfig.d fragments)
4.5 control plane (the plugin dirs). 2a G8: covers plugin/ and plugins/ (both load plugins, spike B 1b); the id is unchanged

gate_rules.hint: A gated command name comes from a variable, substitution or `eval`; write the command out literally.
Do not run git or gh from an interpreter script (`python -c`, `sh -c`, ...); run the command directly.
This git alias cannot be resolved safely (shell alias, cycle, too deep or unknown directory); use the real subcommand.
The command cannot be parsed safely (over 1 MiB, NUL bytes, invalid UTF-8, an unterminated quote, nesting that is too deep, or a brace or glob that expands to too many names).

human_identity.note: Plan 006 K2 (narrowed by the maintainer): values that mean git had no real human identity. carter-bot@* is the old default email on its own; the state-commit fallback is the PAIR name Carter + state@carter.invalid (each alone is a valid identity). Rendered into the guard script at install; tests/data/human_identity_vectors.json is the shared oracle.
